# Digital-Tool @ Stage 9 — Primary / Modern

## Expression on this line

Digital-tool at Order 7 is **systematic tool design**: the deliberate construction of
tool systems based on explicit principles. "I design this tool because I have reasoned
about it" — tool design is self-authored rather than inherited. The designer who
constructs a systematic interface, the engineer who builds a digital system, the
educator who designs a technology curriculum — these are Stage 9 tool architects.

The key advance from Stage 8 is **systemic tool modeling**. The agent does not just
see multiple perspectives on tools — it sees how tool designs interact as a dynamic
system with feedback loops, emergent properties, and structural constraints.

Tool use at Stage 9 is understood as **designable**. The agent believes that tool
design can be intentionally improved through rational analysis and systematic design.
This is the modernist tool design: interfaces are engineering problems that can be
solved with the right design.

But tool reasoning at Stage 9 is still **framework-bound**. The agent designs tool
systems within a particular framework (user-centered, systems, cognitive) but cannot
step outside the framework to evaluate it.

The transition from Stage 9 to Stage 10 occurs when the agent can evaluate entire
tool frameworks.

In human development, Stage 9 corresponds to the professional who can construct and
defend a systematic tool design theory.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Institutional tool design culture emerges. Universities, design institutes,
  tool research centers.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and evaluate tool systems using explicit
  principles.

- **LL:** Systemic tool institutions emerge: design standards, usability testing
  methodologies, tool research centers.

- **LR:** The university, the design lab, the tool research institute.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Methodological hubris — the belief that one's tool design
  approach is objectively true and all others are wrong.

- **Dark allergy:** Anti-design nihilism — the rejection of all systematic tool
  reasoning.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to systematic tool reasoning as the only valid
  approach.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting systematic tool design as dehumanizing.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Systemic tool modeling:** The agent can trace tool dynamics and predict how
  changes affect system behavior.

- **Design-based tool reasoning:** The agent proposes tool improvements based on
  analysis.

- **Framework-bound analysis:** The agent reasons brilliantly within a tool framework
  but cannot evaluate the framework itself.

- **Expert-dependent design:** Tool design is concentrated in professionals.

## Sources, joints, open questions

- Norman, D.A. (1988). *The Design of Everyday Things* — systematic tool design
- Nielsen, J. (1994). *Usability Engineering* — systematic usability methodology
- Gibson, K.R. (1990). *Tools, Language and Cognition in Human Evolution* — tool
  design as engineering
